jobs.title: Client Success Manager, Enterprise
jobs.description:
About Us

Dorsia is at the forefront of hospitality-tech innovation, redefining how the world gains access to the most in-demand restaurants, events, and experiences. By fusing cutting-edge technology with the art of luxury hospitality, we empower our members to secure impossible-to-get reservations while providing operators with unprecedented levels of control, visibility, and revenue optimization.

In 2025, we grew revenue 480% and scaled to 400+ venues across 25 destinations, with the launch of our Culture Calendar extending Dorsia beyond restaurants into the world's most sought-after cultural moments.

Backed by $54M in funding from investors including Index Ventures, Invus, and Red Sea Ventures, and strategic partners including MoonPay, Major Food Group, and The Dinex Group - Daniel Boulud, we are entering our most consequential phase of growth and reshaping the global hospitality landscape. We're adding exceptional talent to drive what comes next, and that's where you come in.

About the Role

Dorsia is seeking a Client Success Manager, Enterprise to own onboarding and ongoing success for the hospitality partners and private member clubs that run on Dorsia's technology through PMC, our enterprise platform. PMC is an operating system that gives operators the AI infrastructure, CRM, and member tooling built at Dorsia, deployed under their own brand and powered by Dorsia. This is the first client success hire dedicated to PMC, and the function is distinct from our restaurant and events client success teams. The accounts are enterprise, the relationships run for years, and each client's membership business depends on the platform performing from day one.

The Client Success Manager, Enterprise takes each account at contract signing and carries it through kickoff, implementation, and on-site enablement into an ongoing enterprise relationship. Within the first three months, this person will build the enterprise training library, including video walkthroughs and a knowledge base, that becomes the standard for every PMC onboarding that follows. The role works closely with the PMC, product, engineering, and partnerships teams, and requires regular travel to client properties.

The Client Success Manager, Enterprise is obsessed with creating a frictionless, white-glove customer experience. They anticipate what a client needs before the client thinks to ask, handle the details so operators can focus on hospitality, and treat every onboarding with the care of a property opening.

What You’ll Do

Client Onboarding and Implementation

- Take each new PMC client from signed contract to live, running the kickoff call and setting scope, owners, and success criteria.

- Use agents to ingest and structure each deployment's inputs, from member data and tier logic to brand assets and integration requirements, so every deployment starts from clean data.

- Own the implementation timeline against committed go-live dates and keep the client and internal teams aligned on every milestone.

- Lead on-site enablement at client properties, training leadership, membership, and front of house teams on the platform and the workflows it replaces.

- Treat every onboarding as a launch with a date attached, not a checklist worked at leisure.

Training and Enablement

- Build the PMC training library from the ground up, including video walkthroughs, a knowledge base, and role-specific onboarding paths.

- Build agents that draft, update, and version training content from each product release, so documentation ships the same week the feature does.

- Turn recurring client questions into self-serve resources and agent-ready knowledge that resolves them before they become tickets.

- Design enablement to compound, so each new client goes live faster than the last.

Account Management and Platform Support

- Serve as the day-to-day owner for an assigned book of PMC clients and resolve issues and escalations within SLA.

- Act as the first credible filter between a client and the product and engineering teams, using agents to triage, reproduce, and document issues, and owning follow-through back to the client.

- Keep clients current on new platform capability and translate each release into what it changes for their members and staff.

- Build relationships with the GM, membership leadership, and ownership group at each account, and anticipate needs before they surface.

Client Success Operations and Reporting

- Write the PMC client success playbook, including onboarding stages, SLAs, health scoring, growth strategy and escalation paths.

- Run the function AI-native, deploying agentic workflows across account research, client communication, meeting capture, and reporting.

- Track adoption, member engagement, and account health, and feed renewal, expansion, and churn signals into leadership reporting.

- Bring field feedback to product that is specific enough to shape the PMC roadmap.

The Winning Recipe

- Bachelor's degree in Business, Hospitality, Communications, or a related field.

- 3-5 years in enterprise SaaS enablement, implementation, or client success, with a strong operational component to the work.

- Proven experience building agents and automating workflows beyond just AI usage.

- Experience selling, onboarding, or enabling enterprise platforms that clients run their core operations on.

- A systems thinker who sees the pattern behind the problem and builds processes that make each onboarding smoother than the last.

- An owner and a solution seeker who handles every account with white glove quality service, caring deeply about details, never taking no as a final answer, and fixing problems before anyone notices.

- Able to travel to client properties as onboardings require.

- Experience building a playbook and function from scratch is a plus.

- Hospitality experience, particularly hotels or membership-driven businesses, is a plus.

Compensation:

New York Pay Range
$80,000 — $110,000 USD

Workplace Philosophy at Dorsia

At Dorsia, we believe that culture eats strategy. The best ideas in the world mean nothing without the right people around the table and the right chemistry between them. We are, unapologetically, a people-first organization.

In-Person Matters

We’re creating once-in-a-lifetime experiences for the most discerning audience in the world. That doesn’t happen over Zoom. It happens through collisions: a spark across a desk, a kitchen-side conversation that unlocks a partnership, the energy of ideas felt, not typed. That’s why in-office culture is non-negotiable at Dorsia.

Who We Hire

We don’t subscribe to check-the-box hiring. We hire for merit and mindset, which naturally creates a team with varied backgrounds. What unites us isn’t demographics, it’s a shared vision: to build the social operating system for the cultural vanguard.

Lifestyle Hours

We’re not a 9-to-5 company. Our lifestyle mirrors our members. Early flights, after-work events, and late-night sprints when the work demands it. But we love what we do, and we definitely love a good party.

High Performance Culture

Working at Dorsia isn’t for everyone—and that’s the point. Our culture is designed for builders, not passengers. We move fast, set ambitious standards, and expect people to rise to them. If you have the talent and the drive, this will be a ride to remember.

A Final Word

We’re building something special. It will take long hours and relentless effort. It’s not for everyone. For those with the metabolism, you’ll create something that changes how culture is lived. And that’s the kind of work worth your life’s energy.

jobs.title: Director of Partnerships
jobs.location: Miami, FL or New York, NY
jobs.description:

About the Role

Dorsia is seeking a Director of Partnerships to own the function that turns partner interest into signed, operationalized revenue. This role owns every partnership and sponsorship deal end to end, from first call through go-live, across member inventory, event technology, and brand sponsorship, and brings finance, legal, marketing, product, and operations in at the right moments rather than after the fact. This is a role for someone who individually closes deals and stays with them until they are live.

The right candidate has run partnerships end to end at a consumer, media, or hospitality business and knows the difference between a partnership that reads well in a deck and one a venue team can deliver on a Saturday night. Dorsia's inventory is scarce by design and every partnership spends some of it, so you will decide what access to the most discerning audience in the world is worth and turn down the deals that would dilute it.

What You’ll Do

Deal Origination & Structuring

- Own every partnership and sponsorship deal from first call through operationalization as the single point of accountability across the company.

- Scope what a partner actually wants across member inventory, event technology, and sponsorship, holding one qualification standard so introductions sourced anywhere in the business enter a single pipeline in a single shape.

- Define what Dorsia will and will not sell against its inventory, and decline the deals that spend scarcity for too little.

- Deploy AI research agents to qualify partners before the first call, surfacing brand fit, audience overlap, and prior activation history so scoping starts from evidence rather than discovery.

Negotiation, Underwriting & Contracting

- Negotiate, draft, and close Dorsia's partner agreements, spanning trademark and IP licensing, member entitlement mechanics, media and co-marketing commitments, exclusivity and category carve-outs, rights of publicity for talent deals, and data sharing terms.

- Design the member entitlement mechanics behind every deal: what the benefit is, which tiers receive it, how it is provisioned and capped, what happens when it is oversubscribed, and when it expires.

- Partner with Finance on economics, margin, and the modeling behind every committed term.

- Run review calls with marketing and product as terms evolve, confirming every promised capability is deliverable before it is signed.

Operationalization & Partner Ownership

- Own the operationalization plan the moment a deal is signed, naming owners, dates, and deliverables across marketing, product, and operations.

- Hand day-to-day execution to the account manager assigned to the partner while remaining the partner's senior point of contact, and intervene the moment promised and delivered begin to diverge.

- Define the renewal and expansion motion, entering every renewal conversation with the performance record already in hand.

- Deploy AI agents to track live deliverables against signed terms across marketing, product, and operations, surfacing slippage the week it happens rather than at the renewal conversation.

Executive Cadence & Pipeline

- Run the weekly partnership review with an agenda that names exactly what is required from finance, marketing, and product on each live deal.

- Bring new partnership opportunities to the executive team with a point of view rather than a menu.

- Own a single source of truth on pipeline, stage, and economics, deploying AI agents to keep deal records, call notes, and stages current without manual entry.

Team & Systems Build

- Build and manage a small team of Partnership Account Managers, setting the standard for how a Dorsia partner is handled.

- Establish the standardized partnership process, intake through renewal, that the company does not have today.

- Produce the deck, proposal, and one-pager templates that make every partner-facing document read as on brand and considered.

- Implement AI agents that draft first-pass proposals, turn partner calls into structured deal notes, and flag at-risk deliverables ahead of a renewal, replacing manual coordination with systems that hold past the next ten deals.

The Winning Recipe

- Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, or related field.

- 7+ years in partnerships, business development, or commercial roles, including 3+ years owning deals end to end through close.

- Direct experience in luxury, hospitality, live events, media, or premium consumer, where the brand across the table is as protective of its image as Dorsia is.

- A closer's record, with specific deals you personally negotiated and signed and terms and economics you can walk through line by line.

- Fluency in commercial structures including rate cards, revenue share, minimum spends, sponsorship packages, and in-kind value.

- Experience building a repeatable partnership process and the materials that go with it, not only operating inside one someone else built.

- Proven people management, with a track record of hiring and developing junior commercial talent.

- A builder's mindset towards AI, with demonstrated experience deploying AI agents and automation across pipeline management, proposal generation, and partner reporting.

- Fluency in CRM and pipeline tooling, contract and e-signature workflows, and BI reporting (i.e. HubSpot, Salesforce, Looker, etc.).

- The judgment to run a cross-functional deal without owning any of the functions, and the standing to hold finance, legal, marketing, and product to dates.

- Comfort with lifestyle hours, since partner dinners, activations, and on-site delivery happen at night and on weekends.

- The discipline to know that growth and exclusivity are not a tradeoff at Dorsia.

- Experience with sponsorship sales or brand activations inside a membership business is a plus.

$140,000 — $180,000 USD
